title: Usage Reassessment Terms of the Security Deposits Tiers
content:
An additional Security Deposits assessment on usage growth is possible only on a tier that allows it. The tier also fixes how far the current average monthly bill must exceed the bill basis of the existing deposit, and the smallest additional deposit that is assessed.

| Tier | Additional deposit on usage growth allowed | Percent by which the current average monthly bill must exceed the existing deposit's bill basis | Smallest additional deposit assessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Standard Deposit | no | 50 | $50.00 |
| Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit | no | 50 | $50.00 |
| Seasonal Residence Deposit | no | 50 | $50.00 |
| Farm Service Deposit | no | 50 | $50.00 |
| General Service Deposit | yes | 25 | $100.00 |
| Irrigation and Large Power Deposit | yes | 25 | $500.00 |

A shortfall smaller than the tier's smallest additional deposit is not assessed. On the four tiers that do not allow reassessment, the percent and minimum figures are listed for completeness but never lead to an additional deposit.

Hypothetical illustration: on the General Service Deposit, an existing deposit computed from a $400.00 basis bill is exceeded by more than 25 percent once the current average monthly bill is above $500.00; at exactly $500.00 it is not exceeded by more than 25 percent.
